content.value_statement: Users often need consistent timestamps for logs, files, and API requests. This skill gives concise date command patterns for local time, UTC, and safe file names.
actual_capabilities: Provides shell date patterns for common calendar formats.
Shows local and UTC ISO 8601 timestamp formats.
Lists format codes for year, month, day, time, and timezone values.
Gives Unix timestamp formats in seconds and milliseconds.
Suggests file-safe timestamp formats for generated names.
Includes examples for log entries, backups, and API timestamps.
limitations: It depends on the local system date command behavior.
It does not calculate future or past dates beyond command examples.
It does not manage timezone databases or daylight saving rules.
Some millisecond formatting may differ across operating systems.

use_cases.title: Create Log Timestamps
use_cases.description: Generate a consistent timestamp format for application logs or operational notes.

use_cases.title: Name Backup Files
use_cases.description: Choose compact date and time formats that work well in file names.

use_cases.title: Prepare API Dates
use_cases.description: Use UTC ISO 8601 timestamps when an API or workflow requires portable time values.

prompt_templates.title: Get Today's Date
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple date value.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the datetime skill to give me today's date in year-month-day format.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Log Timestamp
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for logs or status messages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the datetime skill to format the current local date and time for a log entry.

prompt_templates.title: Build a File Name Timestamp
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the datetime skill to suggest a file-safe timestamp for a backup file name.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Local and UTC Formats
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the datetime skill to show local and UTC timestamp formats for an API integration.

output_examples.input: I need a date for a daily report.
output_examples.output: Use a year-month-day value such as 2026-07-06 for a sortable report date.

output_examples.input: I need a timestamp for logs.
output_examples.output: Use a full timestamp such as 2026-07-06 11:30:00 for readable log entries.

output_examples.input: I need a UTC API timestamp.
output_examples.output: Use a UTC ISO 8601 value such as 2026-07-06T11:30:00Z for portable API requests.

best_practices: Use UTC timestamps for data shared across systems.
Use sortable year-month-day formats for reports and file lists.
Use file-safe formats without spaces or colons for generated file names.
anti_patterns: Do not mix local time and UTC in the same workflow without labels.
Do not use human-readable month names when machines need to sort values.
Do not assume millisecond syntax behaves the same on every operating system.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps format current dates, times, timestamps, and UTC values for common workflow needs.

faq.question: Does it change system time?
faq.answer: No. The examples read the current system time and format it for output.

faq.question: Can it produce UTC timestamps?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes UTC ISO 8601 formats for APIs and cross-timezone workflows.

faq.question: Can it create file-safe names?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows compact formats that avoid spaces and colons in generated names.

faq.question: Does it support Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: What should users verify?
faq.answer: Users should verify local timezone settings and operating system differences before relying on exact output.
